title: Rethinking Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting Evaluation
claim: Method rankings on synthetic benchmarks do not carry over to real-world data, so synthetic evaluation can bias which approach looks best.
layout: 2 grouped bar panels, left-to-right, dashed divider, value labels on bars
description: A single bar chart split by a vertical dashed line into two groups. The left group is titled 'Synthetic Dataset (CiK)' and the right group 'Realistic Dataset (Our TimesX)'. Each group has three bars in the same colors: blue for TimesFM, green for Gemini and red for CodeRev. The y-axis is MASE, with lower being better, and runs from 0.2 to 0.8. Exact values sit above each bar. On the synthetic side the bars fall steeply, from TimesFM at 0.696 to Gemini at 0.316 and CodeRev at 0.241. On the realistic side the bars are nearly level and the order reverses: TimesFM is 0.645, Gemini 0.650 and CodeRev 0.713. The eye goes first to the tall blue bar and the short red bar on the left, then to the reversed pattern on the right. The right title and bar edge look slightly cropped.
caption: Synthetic (CiK) versus real-world (TimesX) performance under the same setup (lower MASE is better). The ordering of TimesFM-2.5, Gemini-2.0-Flash, and CodeRev flips between the two datasets, showing that synthetic generation can bias rankings toward instruction-following LLM and coding. We show results on the Future subset of CiK here. Table 15 further reports the average performance across all subsets with the same conclusion.
abstract: We introduce a new context-enriched, multimodal time series forecasting benchmark, TimesX. TimesX contains a wide selection of high-quality real-world time series with diverse domains and textual contexts obtained from an automated data generation pipeline, which helps address three main issues of existing multimodal forecasting benchmarks: (1) poor generalization due to the small scale and synthetic nature of benchmark data, (2) very limited types of textual contexts in the benchmarks, and (3) an inability to mitigate data leakage in evaluation. We conduct a thorough empirical study of zero-shot multimodal forecasting approaches on TimesX. Our results suggest that many approaches that perform well on existing benchmarks may fail on TimesX. In contrast, simple ensemble methods that leverage rich textual context accompanying time-series can outperform strong baselines on TimesX.
